title: Declared scope directories with write-equal eligibility (I9 findings F1, F2)
summary: UI directories come from the declaration (one directory per alias, the module's model directory as default, empty when none) and offer only what the final write would accept: the same mode, alias, structural, tenant-membership and `allows(Assignment)` checks as `ChangeValidator`, so the P1 findings F1 (directory ignores an effective None mode) and F2 (directory ignores target tenant membership) are gone and the parity matrix reports zero directory/write disagreements.
why: I9 requires directory eligibility to equal write admission (architecture#operation-chains F); P1.3 recorded 82 disagreements with owner P2. Core must stop instantiating the module's `QueryScopeDirectory` (I2). Hard risk: directory and write must share one admission function, otherwise they drift again.

include: `Directories\DirectoryResolver::scopes(alias)` resolves the class-string from `Panel::scopeDeclaration()->directories[alias]` through the container; alias without directory → empty directory; no reference to `QueryScopeDirectory` or `ConfigurableAssignmentScopeDefinition` in core (i2 entries removed)
`ScopesPlugin::register()` contributes `Directories\QueryScopeDirectory` (row relocate P3 keeps its FQCN now) as default directory for its model-backed aliases

One core-internal admission routine (in `Changes` or `Directories` internals) used by `ChangeValidator` final validation and by directory filtering/`describe()`: mode → alias → resolve → structural → target tenant membership → evaluator `allows(phase Assignment|Inspection)`
`QueryScopeDirectory::search()/describe()` consult that routine (or receive pre-filtered candidates) so no offered option is rejected by the write for a scope reason
tests/Fixtures/Parity/i9-findings-0.7.0.json emptied (findings F1, F2 resolved) and ParityMatrixTest asserts zero directory/write disagreements; F1 and F2 cases kept as named regression tests
Migration line: custom directories are declared per alias through the declaration
